The new result is a reusable reaction interface with a certified correlated entrance law

The construction now goes beyond predicting a first reaction. It acquires a compact distribution of the hidden state left by that reaction, certifies the whole distribution, and reuses it to predict a later reaction.

The strongest executed case starts from 73 guarded rules describing a two-state controller and 24 heterogeneous two-state components. The source checker obtains the local operators without constructing the program’s 225=33,554,4322^{25}=33{,}554{,}432225=33,554,432 global configurations. After an observed reaction, a mixture of 256 product distributions represents the correlated entrance state with total-variation error below

3.774×10−9.\boxed{3.774\times10^{-9}}.3.774×10−9​.

That retained distribution has been used in a second calculation. At elapsed time 0.10.10.1, its certified next-reaction probability differs from the prediction obtained by replacing it with the product of its true marginals. The difference survives all the numerical error allowances.

There are also two constructive extensions:

  • An exact filter for changing reaction interfaces preserves a finite correlated preparation mixture across appropriately observed events.
  • A controlled entrance approximation for uncertain event times extends, at the theorem level, to arbitrary finite local continuous-time Markov chains.

The previous three working scripts were present and have been preserved. The source compiler, entrance constructions, proofs and calculations described below are new work in this continuation.

The hidden state after an observed reaction may be correlated even when the underlying components were initially independent. A common unobserved activation time is one mechanism that creates those correlations.

Further conditioning is different. Conditioning on another unlikely observation can amplify error, so it requires a probability or density lower bound. The proofs and implementations keep that distinction explicit.

2. Obtaining the operators from compact rules

The new source_interface_compiler.py accepts a deliberately explicit source language:

  • Boolean sites, equality guards and nonnegative rational rates.
  • Single-site writes for silent transitions.
  • Marked reactions with fixed-write resets.
  • A supplied positive mixture describing initialization.

The controller sites are declared in the input. The compiler checks their autonomy: silent controller rules may read only controller sites. It then obtains the remaining components from the silent read/write scopes and reaction-hazard scopes.

A reaction hazard that touches two residual components causes those components to be merged. If a requested partition separates them, the compiler returns the offending rule and scope. Component-size limits are checked before local enumeration.

A future protocol tied to uncertain absolute time needs the joint time/state information or an additional temporal error bound. Representative timestamps do not certify the continuous clock.
